title: vaderSentimentScores
summary: Score tokenized documents with VADER-style sentiment rules.

gpu_support.notes: `vaderSentimentScores` consumes host tokenizedDocument metadata and returns host score vectors. Resident payloads inside supported objects may gather automatically through their owning provider; the function has no provider kernel.

description: `vaderSentimentScores(documents)` returns a compound sentiment score for each English `tokenizedDocument`. `[compoundScores,positiveScores,negativeScores,neutralScores] = vaderSentimentScores(___)` also returns positive, negative, and neutral proportions.
behaviors: `documents` must be a RunMat `tokenizedDocument` compatibility object with English language metadata.
Compound scores are normalized to the range [-1, 1] from token sentiment values after applying booster, dampener, negation, capitalization, and punctuation modifiers.
`SentimentLexicon` accepts a RunMat table with lowercase string `Token` values and numeric `SentimentScore` values in the documented range [-4, 4].
`SentimentScore` accepts single, double, and all eight native integer classes. Integer scores are range-checked exactly before entering the floating sentiment calculation, and all outputs are double.

`Boosters` and `Dampeners` accept string, character, cell, or string-array inputs. Column vectors are treated as word lists; multi-column string arrays are treated as row-wise n-grams with empty padding ignored.
`Negations` accepts string, character, cell, or string-array word lists.

RunMat ships a compact built-in English compatibility lexicon and modifier lists for common scripts and examples. For domain-specific or full-coverage scoring, pass an explicit `SentimentLexicon` table.
The default lexicon is not yet the complete MATLAB/VADER lexicon, and exact MATLAB VADER scoring parity remains tracked by the broader Text Analytics compatibility issue.

examples.input:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["The book was VERY good!!!!"; "The book was not very good."]);
compoundScores = vaderSentimentScores(documents)
examples.output: `compoundScores` is a numeric column vector with one score per document.
Each output is a numeric column vector with one value per document.
The custom table replaces the built-in compact lexicon.

faqs.question: Does RunMat include MATLAB's full default VADER lexicon?
faqs.answer: Not yet. The builtin includes a compact default compatibility lexicon and fully supports custom lexicon tables.

faqs.question: Are booster, dampener, and negation options supported?
faqs.answer: Yes. `Boosters`, `Dampeners`, and `Negations` are parsed and applied to preceding sentiment-bearing tokens.

faqs.question: Does `vaderSentimentScores` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It performs host text/object processing and returns host numeric score vectors. Supported resident payloads may gather automatically through their owning provider.

example.input:
compoundScores = vaderSentimentScores(documents)
compoundScores = vaderSentimentScores(documents, Name, Value)
[compoundScores,positiveScores,negativeScores,neutralScores] = vaderSentimentScores(___)
example.output: Numeric column vectors with one score per input document.

points: `SentimentLexicon` must be a table with `Token` and `SentimentScore` variables.
`Token` entries in a custom lexicon must be nonempty lowercase strings.
`SentimentScore` entries must be finite single, double, or native integer values in [-4, 4].
`Boosters`, `Dampeners`, and `Negations` must contain at least one word or n-gram when supplied.

gpu_residency: `vaderSentimentScores` operates on host tokenizedDocument objects and has no provider-resident kernel.
